rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads Lord of the worlds as an argument for the ancient God's existence; the created lights, darkness, and angels are kinds within that all-encompassing world-order.
rows.anchor: وهذه أسرار عجيبة ولطائف عالية ؛ إلا أنها بأسرها تجري مجرى الأنواع الداخلة تحت البحر الأعظم المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because worlds include everything besides God, including space and time, their Lord created them and existed before them; this proves His transcendence beyond place, direction, and spatial extension.
rows.anchor: ﴿ رب العالمين ﴾ يدل على كونه ربا للمكان والزمان وخالقا لهما وموجدا لهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same lordship excludes indwelling: the creator precedes every created locus and therefore never depends on a place, against Christians and adherents of indwelling.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أن إله العالم ليس موجبا بالذات بل هو فاعل مختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deserving praise shows God acts by choice, not by necessity: fire and ice are not praised for natural effects, while changing effects prove a voluntary, powerful agent.
rows.anchor: فلما حكم بكونه مستحقا للحمد والثناء ثبت أنه فاعل بالاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The world's evident order and its fitness for human interests show that its maker knows; praise thus implies God's existence, transcendence from place and indwelling, and utmost power, knowledge, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: كان الإحكام والإتقان ظاهرين في العالم الأعلى والعالم الأسفل وفاعل الفعل المحكم المتقن يجب أن يكون عالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In prosperity, God's creation supplies safety and honor; in affliction, He either vindicates victims on Judgment Day or rewards what He sent, so He merits limitless praise.
rows.anchor: فإن كانت من العباد فالله سبحانه وتعالى وعد بأنه ينتصف للمظلومين في يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence Lord of the worlds, Merciful, Compassionate, Master of Judgment is, in Razi's view, a rationally unsurpassable ordering of God's attributes.
rows.anchor: مرتب ترتيبا لا يمكن في العقل وجود كلام أكمل وأفضل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi moves from lordship to servitude: the body is an instrument for the soul, and worship is its best state and the first stage of human felicity; divine aid and guidance are the next stages.
rows.anchor: فأحسن أحوال العبد في هذه الدنيا أن يكون مواظبا على العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path in belief avoids both excessive transcendence, which negates attributes, and excessive affirmation, which anthropomorphizes; it affirms without either error.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم الإقرار الخالي عن التشبيه والتعطيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Regarding human acts, the middle position affirms human agency while holding that all occurs by God's decree, avoiding both Qadari determinism of human independence and denial of agency.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم إثبات الفعل للعبد مع الإقرار بان الكل بقضاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In conduct, the straight path is moderation: chastity between indulgence and rigid abstinence, and courage between recklessness and cowardice.
rows.anchor: والصراط المستقيم هو الوسط وهو العفة وأيضا من بالغ في الأعمال الغضبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path has a positive side, following those God favored—prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous—and a negative side, avoiding those corrupted in practice or belief.
rows.anchor: صراط الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say specifying the path of the favored shows that a seeker needs a guiding shaykh, since most people lack sound judgment and need a perfected guide's intellect.
rows.anchor: إنه لما قال ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ لم يقتصر عليه بل قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the surah sets out the covenants of lordship and servitude together, as in God's promise to fulfill each side of His covenant.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة وافية ببيان ما يجب معرفته من عهد الربوبية وعهد العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the world contains evil, good predominates: health over illness, satiety over hunger, and ease and joy over painful states.
rows.anchor: الشر وإن كان كثيرا إلا أن الخير أكثر والمرض وإن كان كثيرا إلا أن الصحة أكثر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing states arise after nonexistence and therefore point to a capable creator; a necessary-by-nature cause would produce effects eternally without change.
rows.anchor: حدوث الأثر بعد عدمه يدل على وجود مؤثر قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since beneficial ease and safety predominate, the agent is merciful and beneficent and deserves praise; these familiar facts make the reason for praising God apparent to every rational person.
rows.anchor: ومن كان غالب أفعاله راحة وخيرا وكرامة وسلامة كان رحيما محسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All worlds share the contingency, need, and change that make a person depend on God; their common cause of need establishes God's lordship over every creature and heaven.
rows.anchor: وهذه المعاني قائمة في كل العالمين فإنها محل الحركات والسكنات وأنواع التغيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one able to create the immense worlds, Throne, heavens, and stars can destroy them and is independent of them.
rows.anchor: لا بد وأن يكون قادرا على إهلاكها ولا بد وأن يكون غنيا عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy calms the weak servant's awe: worldly life brings continuing mercies, while after death good is repaid without limit and sin may meet pardon and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فأنا الرحمن الرحيم وأنا مالك يوم الدين فما دمت في هذه الحياة الدنيا لا أخليك عن أقسام رحمتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi maps worship to three stages: outward observance is the law, seeking the unseen through divine support is the path, and seeing all affairs as God's is the reality.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يواظب على الأعمال الظاهرة وهو قوله ﴿ إياك نعبد ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A single soul is weaker than many united souls; joining the purified spirits seeking spiritual disclosures strengthens readiness to attain the path of those favored.
rows.anchor: فلهذا قال : ﴿ صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Connection with purified spirits increases strength, while connection with evil spirits brings failure and deprivation; Razi identifies those under wrath as immoral people and the astray as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وهم الفساق : ﴿ ولا الضالين ﴾ وهم الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law, path, and reality complete human ascent: worship, reliance on God, and guidance culminate in fellowship with the pure and distance from the wretched.
rows.anchor: أعني الشريعة المدلول عليها بقوله إياك نعبد والطريقة المدلول عليها بقوله وإياك نستعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because worldly benefits and protection from harm usually require visible causes, people love those causes, and repeated action and imitation make this attachment deeply rooted.
rows.anchor: الأسباب الموجبة لحب الدنيا والمرغبة في التعلق بأسبابها كثيرة قوية شديدة جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi frames the needed reflection as asking whether a ruler's worldly sovereignty came from his own strength and wisdom.
rows.anchor: هذا الأمير المستولي على هذا العالم استولى على الدنيا بفرط قوته وكمال حكمته أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruler may be weak and unintelligent, so his authority comes from the allotment of a wise determiner, not his own strength or wisdom.
rows.anchor: ذلك الأمير ربما كان أكثر الناس عجزا وأقلهم عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognizing the true cause detaches the heart from apparent means: every benefit comes from God and every harm is attributed to Him, so praise and requests belong to God alone.
rows.anchor: كلما وصل إليه نفع وخير قال هو النافع وكلما وصل إليه شر ومكروه قال هو الضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection scales from the small world to the greater one: no condition in either world is ordered except by God's decree.
rows.anchor: ثم يترقى من العالم الصغير إلى العالم الكبير فيعلم أنه لا تنتظم حالة من أحوال العالم الأكبر إلا بتقدير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmos is ordered with optimal perfection, and even atoms testify to God's mercy, favor, and beneficence, leading the servant to call Him Merciful and Compassionate.
rows.anchor: منظومة على الوصف الأتقن والترتيب الأقوم والكمال الأعلى والمنهج الأسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concern about death is eased by recognizing that the Master of Judgment is the same merciful Lord who repairs the servant's needs in both lives.
rows.anchor: مالك يوم الدين ليس إلا الذي عرفته بأنه الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the servant ceases serving rulers and relying on them for wealth or rank, he turns instead to worshipping God and seeking guidance and knowledge from Him.
rows.anchor: فعند زوال ذلك التعلق يعلم أنه لما كان مشتغلا بخدمة الأمير والوزير فلأن يشتغل بخدمة المعبود كان أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity divides between those who serve, rely on, and seek good from God and those who depend on people; the servant asks to join the favored, not the lost parties.
rows.anchor: إلهي اجعلني في زمرة الفرقة الأولى وهم الذين أنعمت عليهم بهذه الأنوار الربانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the second, misguided party brings loss and destruction; Razi introduces the Quranic rebuke against worshipping what cannot hear, see, or help.
rows.anchor: فإن متابعة هذه الفرقة لا تفيد إلا الخسار والهلاك كما قال إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars require recitation in prayer, while al-Asamm and al-Hasan b. Salih deny that recitation is obligatory.
rows.anchor: أجمع الأكثرون على أن القراءة واجبة في الصلاة وعن الأصم والحسن بن صالح أنها لا تجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to perform the dawn recitation in Quran 17:78 is a command to read and therefore makes recitation obligatory.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالقرآن : القراءة والتقدير : أقم قراءة الفجر وظاهر الأمر للوجوب

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي
rows.claim: A man asked the Prophet whether prayer includes recitation; when the man concluded that it was obligatory, the Prophet approved him.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء : أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : أفي الصلاة قراءة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود عن النبي
rows.claim: In another report, the Prophet answers a question about reciting in prayer by asking whether there can be prayer without recitation.
rows.anchor: الثالث : عن ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل : أيقرأ في الصلاة

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm argues that the Prophet described prayer as things seen, whereas recitation is not visible and must therefore fall outside prayer; Razi answers that seeing with two objects means knowing.
rows.anchor:
حجة الأصم قوله - عليه الصلاة والسلام -
: صلوا كما رأيتموني أصلي جعل الصلاة من الأشياء المرئية والقراءة ليست بمرئية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i and most scholars require al-Fatiha itself; omitting even one letter knowingly invalidates prayer, whereas Abu Hanifa says it is not required.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي - رحمه الله - : قراءة الفاتحة واجبة في الصلاة فإن ترك منها حرفا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's lifelong practice of reciting al-Fatiha obligates imitation, supported by Quranic commands to follow him.
rows.anchor: أنه - عليه الصلاة والسلام - واظب طول عمره على قراءة الفاتحة في الصلاة ؛ فوجب أن يجب علينا ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi charges Abu Hanifa with inconsistency for requiring forehead wiping from one report while denying al-Fatiha's requirement despite its mass-transmitted practice.
rows.anchor: تمسك في وجوب مسح الناصية بخبر واحد وذلك ما رواه المغيرة بن شعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the established form of the Prophet's prayer included al-Fatiha, the command to establish prayer requires it; the command recurs over a hundred times in the Quran.
rows.anchor: والتي أتى بها الرسول - عليه الصلاة والسلام - هي الصلاة المشتملة على الفاتحة فيكون قوله : أقيموا الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rightly guided caliphs consistently recited al-Fatiha; reports in both Sahihs say the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar began recitation with al-Hamd, so their practice should be followed.
rows.anchor: روي في الصحيحين أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبا بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما كانوا يستفتحون القراءة بالحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi criticizes Abu Hanifa for relying on Uthman's report in the fugitive-divorce issue despite contrary Companions and Quran, but not following all Companions' practice on al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: أنه تمسك في مسألة طلاق الفار بأثر عثمان مع أن عبد الرحمن وعبد الله بن الزبير كانا يخالفانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims everywhere recite al-Fatiha in prayer; even if some regard it as recommended rather than obligatory, abandoning the unanimous practice leaves the believers' path and incurs Quran 4:115's warning.
rows.anchor: فإنك لا ترى أحدا من المسلمين في المشرق والمغرب إلا ويقرأ الفاتحة في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer's two halves arise through the verses of al-Fatiha; since prayer entails this division and it entails this surah, al-Fatiha is necessary for valid prayer.
rows.anchor: الصلاة لا تنفك عن هذا التنصيف وهذا التنصيف لا يحصل إلا بسبب هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the objection that the negation in no prayer except with al-Fatiha must mean incompleteness rather than invalidity, Razi cites a version explicitly denying prayer's occurrence for one who omits it.
rows.anchor: الأول : أنه جاء في بعض الروايات : لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If al-Fatiha is a constituent of prayer, omitting it means the prayer's very essence does not exist, so the hadith's negation can remain literal.
rows.anchor: من اعتقد أن قراءة الفاتحة جزء من أجزاء ماهية الصلاة فعند عدم قراءة الفاتحة لا توجد ماهية الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the hadith must be figurative, invalidity is nearer than mere incompleteness because a nonexistent act resembles an invalid act more than a valid but imperfect one; presumption, prohibition, and caution reinforce this reading.
rows.anchor: فكان حمل اللفظ على نفي الصحة أولى

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says a prayer without al-Fatiha is deficient and incomplete; Razi argues that a deficient performance does not discharge the continuing obligation.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : كل صلاة لم يقرا فيها بفاتحة الكتاب فهي خداج غير تمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi compares Abu Hanifa's ruling that an Eid fast cannot make up Ramadan because it is incomplete and asks why the same reasoning does not invalidate prayer without al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: فلم لم يقل بمثل هذا الكلام في هذا المقام

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر عن أبي هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits from Abu Huraira that the Prophet said a prayer without al-Fatiha does not suffice.
rows.anchor: عن ابن المنذر أنه روى بإسناده عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : لا تجزىء صلاة

rows.speaker: رفاعة بن مالك عن النبي
rows.claim: A man who asks the Prophet to teach him prayer is told to face the qibla, say takbir, and recite al-Fatiha; Razi treats this imperative as obligation and recitation as part of prayer.
rows.anchor: روى رفاعة بن مالك أن رجلا دخل المسجد وصلى فلما فرغ من صلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies al-Fatiha as a surah unmatched in the Torah, Gospel, or Psalms; the Companions' answer about what they recite in prayer indicates a known universal practice.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ألا أخبركم بسورة ليس في التوراة ولا في الإنجيل ولا في الزبور مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that Quran 73:20 requires al-Fatiha: the options are al-Fatiha, another surah, or a choice; the latter two fail because another is not universally required and al-Fatiha is agreed better and more complete.
rows.anchor: فنقول : المراد بما تيسر من القرآن إما أن يكون هو الفاتحة أو غير الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatiha is the recitation made accessible to all because every Muslim has it memorized, whereas other surahs may not be memorized by each person.
rows.anchor: لأن هذه السورة محفوظة لجميع المكلفين من المسلمين فهي متيسرة للكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original duty to pray remains until evidence shows discharge; al-Fatiha is superior and makes prayer more complete, so omitting it does not establish discharge.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الثابت البقاء خالفنا هذا الأصل عند الإتيان بها للصلاة المشتملة على قراءة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although belief in obligation may itself leave theoretical doubt, actual recitation creates no danger while omission creates fear of failing the duty; therefore action is the safer course.
rows.anchor: أما في العمل فإن القراءة لا توجب الخوف أما تركه فيفيد الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If prayers with and without al-Fatiha were both valid, habitual recitation would make other surahs abandoned; because the community agrees al-Fatiha is preferable, Razi concludes omission is invalid.
rows.anchor: لكنهم أجمعوا على أن الصلاة بهذه السورة أولى فثبت أن الصلاة بغير هذه السورة غير جائزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as bowing and prostration cannot be replaced, al-Fatiha cannot be replaced by another reading, with caution as the common rationale.
rows.anchor: أجمعنا على أنه لا يجوز إبدال الركوع والسجود بغيرهما فوجب أن لا يجوز إبدال قراءة الفاتحة بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty to pray persists; neither Quran 73:20 nor analogy proves discharge without al-Fatiha, and ritual worship is a domain where analogy should be set aside.
rows.anchor: لأن التعبدات غالبة على الصلاة وفي مثل هذه الصورة يجب ترك القياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet recited al-Fatiha throughout his life, replacing it with another recitation is innovation and abandonment of the required prophetic example.
rows.anchor: فحينئذ تكون قراءة غير الفاتحة ابتداعا وتركا للاتباع وذلك حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer without al-Fatiha loses an agreed extra virtue without compensation, which Razi regards as improper and therefore impermissible.
rows.anchor: الصلاة بدون الفاتحة توجب فوات الفضيلة الزائدة من غير جابر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Huraira reports that the Prophet ordered him to announce that there is no prayer without recitation, even if by al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أنه قال : أمرني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أخرج وأنادي : لا صلاة إلا بقراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers Quran 73:20 by the same three options: al-Fatiha itself, another passage, or a choice; the latter two fail, and al-Fatiha is accessible to all.
rows.anchor: فنقول : المراد بما تيسر من القرآن : إما أن يكون هو الفاتحة أو غير الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi counters the opposing report with Abu Huraira's version no prayer except by al-Fatiha; if reports conflict, the stronger and safer view is his.
rows.anchor: معارض بما نقل عن أبي هريرة أنه قال أمرني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أخرج وأنادي لا صلاة إلا بفاتحة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reports disagreement over the minimum recitation for Hanafis: Abu Hanifa accepts one verse, even isolated letters, while Abu Yusuf and Muhammad require three short verses or one long verse.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : إذا قرأ آية واحدة كفت مثل قوله آلم وحم والطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i says the basmala is a verse of al-Fatiha and must be read; Malik and al-Awza'i exclude it except in the Quran's Naml passage, with a Ramadan-night exception, while Abu Hanifa orders quiet recitation without stating its status.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية من أول سورة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: يعلى
rows.claim: The narrator reports asking Muhammad b. al-Hasan whether the basmala is Quran, introducing a discussion of its legal status.
rows.anchor: قال يعلى سألت محمد بن الحسن عن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فقال

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr calls the basmala's Quranic status categorical: error is at least sinful, since its inclusion must be proved by mass transmission, not a solitary report.
rows.anchor: وزعم القاضي أبو بكر أنها من المسائل القطعية قال : والخطأ فيها إن لم يبلغ إلى حد التكفير

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali counters that denying the basmala's Quranic status faces the same proof dilemma; although absence is the default, its Quranic-script inscription requires separate evidence.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الشيخ الغزالي عارض القاضي فقال : نفي كون التسمية من القرآن إن ثبت بالتواتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says transmission establishes that the basmala was revealed to Muhammad and written in Quranic script; inclusion matters only for legal rulings such as prayer, recitation in impurity, and touching the codex, which are ijtihadi, so the issue is not categorical.
rows.anchor: والذي عندي فيه أن النقل المتواتر ثابت بأن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم كلام أنزله الله على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the report from Umm Salama an explicit text supporting the basmala inclusion in al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وهذا نص صريح . الحجة الثانية :

rows.speaker: أم سلمة عن النبي
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited al-Fatiha while counting the basmala as its first verse, followed by the rest of its verses.
rows.anchor: روى الشافعي رضي الله عنه عن مسلم عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة عن أم سلمة أنها قالت

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Abu Huraira reports the Prophet saying that al-Fatiha has seven verses and the first is the basmala.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد المقبري عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : فاتحة الكتاب سبع آيات أولاهن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: أبو بريدة عن أبيه عن النبي
rows.claim: In al-Tha'labi's report, the Prophet tells Abu Burda that he alone after Solomon received an ayah, then links it to the basmala used to begin Quran recitation and prayer.
rows.anchor: روى الثعلبي في تفسيره بإسناده عن أبي بريدة عن أبيه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the seven oft-repeated verses as al-Fatiha and answers that its seventh verse is the basmala.
rows.anchor: فأين السابعة ؟ فقال : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: A report from Abu Huraira says the Prophet told believers not to omit the basmala when reciting the Mother of the Book because it is one of its verses.
rows.anchor: أنه قال إذا : قرأتم أم القرآن فلا تدعوا بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فإنها إحدى آياتها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: In the divided-prayer report, God calls the basmala glorification, al-Hamd praise, the two mercy names extolling, the Master of Judgment entrustment, and the remaining response a sharing and a request granted.
rows.anchor: فإذا قال العبد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال الله سبحانه مجدني عبدي وإذا قال الحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
rows.claim: Another report says the Prophet rebuked a worshipper who began al-Fatiha without the basmala: omitting a verse cuts the prayer, which is invalid without the whole surah.
rows.anchor: يا رجل قطعت على نفسك الصلاة أما علمت أن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من الحمد

rows.speaker: طلحة بن عبيد الله عن النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever omits the basmala has omitted a verse from God's Book.
rows.anchor: عن طلحة بن عبيد الله قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : من ترك بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that if reading the basmala at the start of al-Fatiha is obligatory, it must be one of its verses; Quran 96:1 commands reading in God's name and the letter has meaning.
rows.anchor: بيان الأول قوله تعالى : ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك ﴾ [ العلق : 1 ] ولا يجوز أن يقال : الباء صلة زائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the basmala is written in Quranic script, while headings and division marks were kept out to prevent mixing non-Quranic text, its inscription marks it as Quran.
rows.anchor: التسمية مكتوبة بخط القرآن وكل ما ليس من القرآن فإنه غير مكتوب بخط القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Muslims agree that everything between the two covers is God's speech and the basmala is there, Razi counts it as divine speech; he notes this does not refute Abu Bakr al-Razi's view that it is Quran only as a surah divider.
rows.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أن ما بين الدفتين كلام الله والتسمية موجودة بين الدفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven-verse count supports al-Shafi'i's division, with the basmala as one verse and the final phrase as one; Abu Hanifa denies the basmala verse and splits that final phrase, a weak view for Razi.
rows.anchor: وسنبين في مسألة مفردة أن قول أبي حنيفة مرجوح ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abu Hanifa agrees the basmala is preferable and the Prophet likely recited it, following him makes it obligatory; with no accepted distinction, it must be part of al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وإذا ثبت وجوب قراءتها ثبت أنها من السورة لأنه لا قائل بالفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's saying that an important matter begun without God's name is cut off implies that prayer, the greatest act after faith, is gravely deficient without the basmala; such acknowledged deficiency entails invalidity.
rows.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه باسم الله فهو أبتر أو أجذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severity of abtar is shown by Quran 108:3, where God calls the Prophet's enemy cut off; thus prayer without the basmala is gravely defective and invalid.
rows.anchor: فلزم أن يقال : الصلاة الخالية عن قراءة بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم تكون في غاية النقصان والخلل

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب عن النبي
rows.claim: When Ubayy b. Ka'b names the basmala as the greatest ayah and the Prophet confirms him, Razi argues it must be a complete ayah somewhere other than its partial appearance in Solomon's letter, namely at al-Fatiha's start.
rows.anchor: ما روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي بن كعب : ما اعظم آية في كتاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muawiya omitted the basmala aloud in prayer, the Migrants and Helpers rebuked him and he repeated the prayer; Razi takes this as Companion consensus that it is Quran and part of al-Fatiha, and that aloud recitation is preferable.
rows.anchor: فلما قضى صلاته ناداه المهاجرون والأنصار من كل ناحية أنسيت ؟ أين بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم حين استفتحت القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that Noah began boarding the Ark in God's name and Solomon's letter began with the basmala; following earlier prophets and then the Prophet makes its recitation obligatory for Muslims and part of al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: أن نوحا عليه السلام لما أراد ركوب السفينة قال : ﴿ اركبوا فيها بسم الله مجراها ومرساها ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the suggestion that Solomon put his own name before God's: the hoopoe laid the letter on the queen, who first identified its sender as Solomon and only after opening it read the basmala.
rows.anchor: فلما فتحت الكتاب رأت التسمية مكتوبة فقالت : وإنه بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God exists before all created things, rational propriety requires mentioning Him before others; what Muslims deem good is good before God, so the basmala should precede recitation and belongs to al-Fatiha.
rows.anchor: والقديم الخالق يجب أن يكون سابقا على المحدث المخلوق وإذا ثبت أنه تعالى سابق على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the basmala unquestionably appears in Quran 27:30 and recurs in Quranic script, Razi argues every occurrence is Quran, by analogy with repeated Quranic refrains.
rows.anchor: أن بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم لا شك أنه من القرآن في سورة النمل ثم إنا نراه مكررا بخط القرآن
